solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Take over from endlessly flexible worker

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word for flexible is dropped

parts.note: supple means flexible or bendy
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A bendy employee is lined up to replace someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp or replace someone in their position is to take over from them.

clue.text: Disgrace, having no time for Greek character

indicators.note: the word lacks one letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: A Greek is ashamed, with no time for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Sounds like an insignificant item of female attire

definitions.text: Sounds like an insignificant item of female attire

parts.words: Sounds like an insignificant item of female attire
parts.note: said aloud the word suggests a petty, trivial coat, yet it is a woman's underskirt

explanation.definitionFit: A petticoat is a woman's slip or underskirt worn beneath a dress.

clue.text: Dabbler and a friend going to ancient city

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A hobbyist and a pal head off to visit ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional who tries things casually is a dabbler.

clue.text: Holy orders

parts.note: the phrase normally means ordination as a priest, but here it is commands given by God

explanation.definitionFit: The laws given to Moses on Sinai are sacred commands, orders from on high.

clue.text: Irregular money order

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A banker's draft looks strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money order' reads as one financial document but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard, following no pattern, is irregular.

clue.text: Like the Tin Man, mug with twitch — 'O my heart!'

indicators.note: the letter goes into the centre of the other pieces

parts.note: to mug someone is to rob them
a tic is a nervous twitch
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Tin Man of Oz, who longed for a heart, cries out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tin Man in The Wizard of Oz wanted a heart, so O fills the heart of ROBTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tin Man is a mechanical man, rather like an automaton.

clue.text: Less than a full team play out miniature scene

indicators.note: the play lies outside, around the other piece

parts.note: a drama is a play
a football or cricket team has eleven players; ten, one short, is written IO, like the digits 10

explanation.surface: A depleted side stages a small-scale show.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional model showing a scene in small scale.

clue.text: Nearly everyone having greatest importance

definitions.meaning: the bulk of the people, almost all of them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means either the majority of people or more than anything else.

clue.text: Woman goes round new border village

indicators.note: the woman's name surrounds the other letter, as if walking round it

parts.note: Greta is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman walks a circuit of a new frontier settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: GRETNA Green is the Scottish village just over the English border, famous for runaway weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gretna sits right on the Scotland-England border, a village known for eloping couples.

clue.text: Hazy blue liquid no American has consumed

indicators.note: the outer pair of words swallows the rearranged letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something liquid flows freely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vague blue fluid that no American has drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' makes EBUL, which slips in after the first letter of the outer pair; 'consumed' says the outer words eat it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nebulous is cloudy or vague, the way a hazy outline is.

clue.text: Central figure that's not unusual being into hare coursing

definitions.text: Central figure that's not unusual being

indicators.note: hares running about in a hare hunt, so the letters chase around into a new order

explanation.surface: Hunting with hounds is not the usual pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: An antihero is the protagonist who is not the usual heroic type, so the definition plays on 'not unusual' twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist who lacks the usual heroic qualities is the central figure of a story without being a classic hero.

clue.text: Island also has land in the interior

indicators.note: the second word is placed inside the first

parts.note: too means also
to land a prize is to bag it

explanation.surface: An island also possesses territory inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in landing or bagging a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, partner of Trinidad.

clue.text: Photo's empty, we hear that adds weight

indicators.note: signals that a word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: hollow means empty
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A picture lacks substance, people say, yet it adds weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A hologram is a three-dimensional photographic image made with lasers.

clue.text: Henry taking steps in the gloaming

parts.note: Hal is a short name for Henry
a flight is a run of stairs

explanation.surface: Henry climbs the stairs at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: The gloaming is the Scots word for twilight, the dim light at dusk.

clue.text: Bounder in Channel Islands with a jumpy creature

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, off the French coast
a bounder or cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: A scoundrel on Jersey or Guernsey alongside a skittish animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' suggests a jumping creature, but it is the old British word for a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is an insect that leaps about and chirps loudly, so a jumping creature.

clue.text: Angry remark that should make you think

parts.note: cross means angry
a word is a brief remark

explanation.surface: A sharp comment ought to give you pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle of clues is meant to make the solver think.

clue.text: That follows coffee before end of dinner

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

indicators.note: takes just the closing letter of the word dinner

explanation.surface: A coffee is served after the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Of two things mentioned, the second one is the one that comes after.

clue.text: VAT guy arrests one driver

indicators.note: catches and holds the other piece inside

parts.note: VAT is UK value added tax, collected by a tax inspector
the roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A tax inspector pulls over a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi driver is a cabbie, someone who drives for hire.

clue.text: Common-sounding element of poetry and slang?

definitions.text: Common-sounding element of poetry and slang?

parts.words: Common-sounding element of poetry and slang?
parts.note: words that share ending sounds feature in verse, and the Cockney slang of London uses that device

explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme is the matching of sounds in verse and in Cockney rhyming slang.

clue.text: Unreal — lotion being smeared round less than half of navel

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the short piece
a lotion spread about is messed up, so its letters are rearranged
keeps only the opening portion, under half, of the word navel

explanation.surface: An imaginary scene of cream being rubbed around a belly button.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being smeared' makes NOTIOL; 'less than half of' keeps NA, two of five letters, which the rearranged lotion goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notional exists only as an idea, in theory, so it is not real.

clue.text: For the audience, draw a number — get tense

indicators.note: the words are taken by how they are heard

parts.note: a draw is a tie, and a number is ten

explanation.surface: Drawing lots before a crowd makes people nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten is to become taut or tense.

clue.text: Leniency is unknown among the non-clerical

indicators.note: the letter sits within the group of people

parts.note: the laity are the ordinary people, not the clergy
x is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Lax behaviour is a mystery to ordinary churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxity is slackness or lack of strictness, much like leniency.

clue.text: Jack played games making the introduction for major celeb

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come first, introducing the other piece
games played about are mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, a tar

explanation.surface: A man named Jack played games before being introduced to a big celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge star of entertainment is a major celebrity.

clue.text: Beam before negative response for send-up material

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

indicators.note: turned upward in a down clue, so read in reverse

parts.note: no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: A beam meets a refusal in a parody of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic fabric made from cellulose.

clue.text: Initiative to stick with small part, backing number one

parts.note: to gum is to stick or glue
pt is the short form of part

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An enterprising actor clings to a minor role while supporting the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing number one' reads as supporting the star, but turns NO and I round to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumption is resourcefulness and get-up-and-go, the same as initiative.

clue.text: Odd characters from town meeting over street heading in opposite directions

indicators.note: takes the first and third letters of town

parts.note: o is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over
way is a word for a road or street, as in Milky Way or Broadway's style names

explanation.surface: Strange folk from town meet up on a road going both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic that runs both ways moves in opposite directions.

clue.text: What one could be doing with a pitch fork

definitions.text: What one could be doing with a pitch fork

parts.words: What one could be doing with a pitch fork
parts.note: a pitchfork is a farm tool for hay, but a fork that gives a musical pitch is used to set an instrument's note

explanation.surface: A farmhand's chores with a hay fork.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuning fork is struck to give a reference pitch when adjusting an instrument.

clue.text: Expelled from university and locked up

definitions.meaning: a British student thrown out of college is said to be rusticated or dismissed
a convict jailed by a judge has been sentenced to prison

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses use the phrasal verb: dismissed from a university, or committed to prison.
